/**
 * @file      enginecapabilities.h
 * @brief     One-shot engine capability probe for the Simulation Options dialog.
 * @author    Caleb Buahin <caleb.buahin@gmail.com>
 * @date      2026
 * @license   GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * One-shot engine capability probe for the Simulation Options dialog.
 *
 * Replaces the in-place `setEnabled()` calls of
 * `SimulationOptionsDialog::applyEngineConstraints()`. Probed once in the
 * dialog constructor and never re-probed: the engine's option surface does not
 * change while a model is open.
 *
 * Each field maps 1:1 onto one `if` block of the original
 * `applyEngineConstraints()`, and each carries a comment naming the block it
 * came from so the port stays auditable (HANDOFF §2.1).
 * @copyright Copyright (c) 2026 Caleb Buahin. All rights reserved.
 */
///< Read-only engine contract; empty on older builds.
///< OPENSWMM_HAS_2D and a non-null engine handle; no mesh query.

/**
 * @brief Snapshot the option-editor capability gates for one engine/version pair.
 * @param e Borrowed valid engine during this read, permitted null.
 * @param version Copied version text; an exact leading 5. marks legacy and
 * short-circuits all probes without trimming or version parsing.
 * @return Owned capability value. Nonlegacy ordinary feature flags require a
 * nonempty successful option read. Implicit-FV support requires parsed schema
 * version one, native true and BACKWARD_EULER integration; parsing retries five
 * buffers from 8 through 128 KiB. Parsed schema is retained even when unsupported.
 * For nonlegacy versions the four legacy-exclusion flags are true even with a
 * null handle. has2D checks only build-time 2D support and a non-null handle, not
 * runtime mesh existence. Does not mutate options, probe again later or own the engine.
 */

/**
 * @file      hydraulicspage.h
 * @brief     Simulation Options → Routing & Hydraulics.
 * @author    Caleb Buahin <caleb.buahin@gmail.com>
 * @date      2026
 * @license   GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * Simulation Options → Routing & Hydraulics.
 *
 * The headline page of the restructure. FLOW_ROUTING sits in a header above
 * the tab bar because it gates three of the four tabs — it can neither live
 * inside one of them nor stay two sidebar rows away on Models / Processes,
 * which is where it used to be (PLAN §2.1).
 *
 * Tabs: Routing · Dynamic Wave · Finite Volume · Unsteady Friction.
 *
 * "Skip steady state" lands on the shared Routing tab rather than Dynamic
 * Wave: SWMMEngine::isInSteadyState() is called from the main routing step
 * with no routing-model guard, so SKIP_STEADY_STATE is honoured under every
 * method (PLAN §7 Q1, resolved by measurement).
 * @copyright Copyright (c) 2026 Caleb Buahin. All rights reserved.
 */

/**
     * @brief Construct routing and hydraulic draft controls from cached engine capabilities.
     * @param ctx Borrowed GUI-thread context that must outlive the page; valid handles
     * and a well-formed implicit schema are required whenever those paths are used.
     * @param parent Optional widget owner; null leaves lifetime to the caller.
     * Builds/tags controls; hydration and applying capability gates are separate.
     */

/**
     * @brief Return the localized sidebar caption.
     * @return Owned Routing & Hydraulics string.
     */

/**
     * @brief Hydrate hydraulic drafts from common options, preferences and fixed solver defaults.
     * Local numeric readers accept a borrowed key plus numeric fallback, returning the
     * converted value or fallback on conversion failure before widget clamping. Combo
     * selector borrows a non-null combo and token, preserving selection on no match;
     * boolean helper maps its scalar to YES/NO. Signals are not blocked, but m_reading
     * suppresses Backward-Euler compatibility resets during hydration. Reads implicit
     * text only when supported, then clears m_reading and refreshes intra-page gates.
     * Does not call option setters, validate the complete draft or save files.
     */

/**
     * @brief Attempt common hydraulic and FV drafts independently through context comparison.
     * @return Successful setter sum; no-op/refusal contributes zero and partial success
     * has no rollback. Writes inactive/disabled solver drafts too; implicit method,
     * preconditioner and text fields are included only when cached support is true.
     * Numeric formatting follows each widget/key precision and implicit text is passed
     * verbatim. SKIP_STEADY_STATE is read/tagged here but is not submitted by this
     * implementation.
     * LAT_FLOW_TOL and SYS_FLOW_TOL are submitted in percent. Does not invoke validate(),
     * create undo or save files; the count does not certify a coherent complete solver setup.
     */

/**
     * @brief Disable unsupported solver choices/controls using the cached capability snapshot.
     * A local helper borrows combo, exact item-data token, tooltip and fallback index;
     * with a standard item model it disables the matching item and changes a currently
     * selected unsupported item to that fallback. Null/nonstandard combos are ignored.
     * FV falls back to dynamic wave, TPA/dynamic slot to EXTRAN and semi-implicit to
     * explicit. Pressure closure/Anderson are disabled where unsupported; UF receives
     * a tooltip while host gates control its tab. Does not re-probe, re-enable choices
     * or write options, though fallback selection can emit normal gate signals.
     */

/**
     * @brief Refresh intra-page controls for the current routing/integration/surcharge drafts.
     * Native Backward Euler under FV enables the schema group/tab and disables explicit
     * performance/reconstruction controls, skip-steady and friction-method selection.
     * Other gates cover DPS/TPA celerity, second-order limiter, LTS tiers, UF coefficient
     * and steady-flow tolerances. Uses cached capability flags; host controls other tabs.
     * Assumes buildUi() completed, does not normalize incompatible drafts or write keys.
     */

/**
     * @brief Check native implicit field input and Backward-Euler compatibility.
     * @param warn Optional borrowed error output, overwritten on the first refusal and
     * left unchanged on success; this method does not append diagnostics.
     * @return True immediately without implicit support. Otherwise false for an active FV
     * Backward-Euler draft with incompatible order/closure/backend/LTS/pressure-only/
     * steady-skip/friction settings, unacceptable schema text or minimum step above
     * maximum. Schema text is checked even when the native integrator is inactive.
     * Requires schema editors for FV_IMPLICIT_MIN_STEP/MAX_STEP; does not repair drafts,
     * validate every explicit hydraulic setting or change engine state.
     */

/**
     * @brief Expose the owned tab container for host gating/navigation.
     * @return Borrowed container; caller must not delete or retain beyond page life.
     */

/**
     * @brief Read the selected routing draft token.
     * @return Owned STEADY, KINWAVE, DYNWAVE or FV item data, or empty without the combo.
     * Does not query engine state or assert that the solver is supported/initialized.
     */

/**
     * @brief Update the minimum-routing-step draft from the performance preset.
     * @param seconds Desired seconds, clamped/rounded by the existing 0.01..360.0,
     * three-decimal spin box. Missing editor is a no-op; does not set MINIMUM_STEP in
     * the engine, change other controls or persist the draft.
     */

/**
     * @brief Create owned hydraulic controls, schema validators and gate connections once.
     * Builds native methods/preconditioners/fields from the cached schema, using integer
     * bounds or C-locale scientific validators with seventeen decimals. Flow/surcharge/
     * order/friction index and LTS/skip toggles ignore scalar arguments and notify host
     * gates; routing has two connections and can notify twice. Selecting Backward Euler
     * outside read() resets pending drafts to first-order SLOT/CPU, LTS/pressure-only/
     * skip-steady off and friction NONE, preserving cell count/celerity; it then refreshes
     * gates and notifies. This is draft normalization, not an engine transaction.
     * Time/decay/minimum-step fields use seconds; flow/slope tolerances use percent and
     * FV cell lengths/celerities use project length units. DPS celerity is displayed m/s.
     * Does not hydrate option values, start a solver or apply drafts.
     */

/**
     * @brief Tag fixed routing/hydraulic controls with their common option keys.
     * Implicit schema widgets are tagged during buildUi(). Tags support reachability
     * inspection and do not themselves prove a corresponding write() call exists.
     */
// project length units; 0 = minimum cell count

 * @file      simulationrunner.cpp
 * @brief     Runs a single SWMM simulation on a worker thread and emits live progress, warnings,
 *            and completion signals back to the GUI thread.

 * @date      2026

/**
 * @brief Probe an existing HDF5 destination for writable lock access without truncating it.
 * @param[in] path Output file path; empty/missing file succeeds without creating it.
 * @param[out] error Busy/access diagnostic on failure, unchanged on success.
 * @return True after a transient platform probe lock is acquired/released, or on platforms without a probe implementation; not a persistent runtime lock.
 */

/**
     * @brief Open an append-only diagnostic log beside the report.
     * @param[in] rptPath Report path defining the .runlog.txt companion stem.
     * @details Open failure leaves logging inert; run output validation/reservations are handled by the caller.
     */

/**
     * @brief Append a timestamped line and request a flush.
     * @param[in] text Diagnostic text.
     * @details No-op when the log is not open; write/flush errors are not propagated. Worker access is serialized by its run.
     */

/**
     * @brief Match a configured test-fault phase exactly.
     * @param[in] p Non-null Latin-1 phase name.
     * @return True for exact configured phase text.
     */

/**
 * @brief Capture snow ledgers on the engine-owning worker and queue copied rows to the GUI.
 * @param[in] self Non-null runner kept alive through worker completion.
 * @param[in] jobId Correlation ID.
 * @param[in] eng Borrowed open worker engine.
 */

/**
 * @brief Queue current solver/backend/tier telemetry when readable.
 * @param[in] self Non-null retained runner receiver.
 * @param[in] jobId Correlation ID.
 * @param[in] eng Borrowed open worker engine; failed stats reads emit nothing.
 * @details At most eight tier counts are copied into the queued value payload.
 */

/**
 * @brief Convert a SWMM engine time (OADate: decimal days since
 *        1899-12-30 00:00:00 nominal calendar) to a QDateTime. Returns an invalid
 *        QDateTime for non-finite or clearly-bogus values (≤ epoch).
 * @param[in] oaDate Positive finite nominal SWMM days since 1899-12-30.
 * @return Shared UTC-basis calendar representation, or invalid for nonpositive/nonfinite input.
 */

/**
 * @brief Find the legacy worker executable for a 5.x engine version.
 *
 * Workers are versioned: `openswmm-legacy-worker-<version>` (the 5.2.4 one is
 * built by cmake/EngineVersions.cmake). The unversioned `openswmm-legacy-worker`
 * the 6.x engine install ships IS the 5.3.0 worker, so it is accepted as a
 * fallback for LEGACY_SWMM_VERSION only — never for any other version, or a
 * missing 5.2.4 worker would silently run the model on 5.3.0.
 *
 * Searches, for each candidate name, in:
 *  1. Same directory as the current executable
 *  2. {app_dir}/bin/{CONFIG}/ (debug/release subdirs)
 *  3. {app_dir}/../bin/{CONFIG}/
 *
 * @return Absolute path to the worker, or an empty string if none was found.
 * @param[in] version Requested legacy version text used in executable names.
 * @details Checks file existence in application/build-relative locations, not PATH or executable permissions. Only the configured LEGACY_SWMM_VERSION may use an unversioned fallback.
 */

/**
 * @brief Remove an unquoted semicolon comment from an INP row.
 * @param[in] line UTF-8-decoded row copied for editing; quote state toggles at each double quote.
 * @return Trimmed content before the first semicolon outside quotes.
 */

/**
 * @brief Split INP option rows using quote-aware whitespace/comma rules.
 * @param[in] line Comment-stripped row text.
 * @return Ordered tokens with surrounding quoted-field delimiters removed; interior commas in whitespace-delimited names are retained. Does not validate balanced quotes.
 */

/**
 * @brief Scan declared built-in input/output resource slots for path protection.
 * @param[in] inp Model file read as UTF-8, with references resolved relative to its directory.
 * @return Owning path lists, empty for unreadable input; does not recurse through arbitrary plugin/nested datasource dependencies.
 */

/**
 * @brief Convert a path to filesystem-native representation.
 * @param[in] path Qt path text.
 * @return Wide Windows or UTF-8 non-Windows filesystem path.
 */

/**
 * @brief Compare file identities without requiring both paths to exist.
 * @param[in] left First path, empty returns false.
 * @param[in] right Second path, empty returns false.
 * @return Filesystem-equivalent/canonically equal or cleaned-absolute-equal paths, case-insensitive on Windows.
 */

/**
 * @brief Translate an escaped worker exception into a terminal failure value.
 * @param[in] phase Last known run phase, or empty for run fallback.
 * @param[in] what Exception description copied into the diagnostic.
 * @param[in] log Optional borrowed log receiving a timestamped exception record.
 * @return Failed result with SWMM_ERR_INTERNAL and captured phase; no engine handles escape.
 */

/**
 * @brief Isolate simulation workers from rendering/IO task starvation.
 * @return Borrowed process-lifetime pool capped at four concurrent run tasks.
 */

/**

                 * @details No-op for null; executes on the engine-owning worker.

/**
 * @file      test_simulationoptions_roundtrip.cpp
 * @author    Caleb Buahin <caleb.buahin@gmail.com>
 * @date      2026
 * @license   GPL-3.0-or-later
 * @brief     Baseline: opening the Simulation Options dialog and pressing Apply
 *         with NO edits must write nothing.
 *
 * This is the safety net for the dialog restructure
 * (workplans/SIMULATION_OPTIONS_AND_PROCESS_GATING_PLAN_2026-09-04.md §3.4,
 * EXECUTION_PLAN_… P0/P3): every page's read()/write() pair must be the
 * identity on an unedited model. Two independent assertions per deck:
 *
 *   1. `wroteAnyChanges()` is false after Apply — the dialog's own dirty count
 *      (writeIfChanged's numeric-aware compare) saw nothing to write.
 *   2. The model serialised BEFORE the dialog existed and AFTER Apply is
 *      byte-identical in every [OPTIONS]-class section — [OPTIONS],
 *      [REPORT], [FILES], [EVENTS], [2D_OPTIONS], [TITLE] — so a write the
 *      dirty count missed (e.g. a value re-formatted to the same number)
 *      still fails here, with a readable diff of the offending section.
 *
 * Decks: a 1D DYNWAVE deck, a 2D deck, and an FV variant derived from the 1D
 * deck (there is no FV fixture yet). All outputs go next to the fixtures
 * (reviewable, CLAUDE.md §4.1).
 * @copyright Copyright (c) 2026 Caleb Buahin. All rights reserved.
 */
